slides.headline: Habits that keep you at *$0*
slides.body: Asking for a friend. The friend is very sure the plan is working.

slides.headline: Rebuilding the stack every *Monday*
slides.body: New framework, new UI kit, same empty inbox. The tool was never the bottleneck.

slides.headline: Polishing the logo, not the *offer*
slides.body: Nobody buys a gradient. They buy a clear answer to "what do I get and what does it cost".

slides.headline: Pricing by *vibes*
slides.body: Picking a number that feels safe instead of asking three people what they would actually pay.

slides.headline: How it feels vs what it *is*
items: "Waiting for the right moment" | Avoiding the DMs
slides.stat: HOW IT FEELS | WHAT IT IS

slides.headline: Shipping ugly beats polishing *invisible*.
slides.body: Forward Thinking Co

slides.headline: Get to your first *yes* faster
slides.body: The starter pack is the checklist these slides wish they'd had.

caption:
Every habit on this list feels productive while you're doing it. That's the problem.

Rebuilding the stack, polishing the logo, waiting for the right moment. None of it puts the offer in front of a person who could say yes.

Pick one habit from this list and drop it this week. Just one.

hook: Brief Claude Code like a client would brief you

slides.headline: Brief Claude Code like a *client* would
Say who it's *for*
slides.body: One sentence: the visitor, what they already tried, and what they want next. Vague audience, vague page.

slides.headline: List the sections in *order*
slides.body: Hero, proof, how it works, offer, FAQ, CTA. Order is a decision. Don't let the model make it for you.

slides.headline: Paste the *real* copy
slides.body: Placeholder text produces placeholder layouts. Give it the actual headline and the actual price, even if rough.

slides.headline: Write the visual *rules* down
slides.body: Two fonts, a few colours, a spacing scale, one accent. Keep them in a file the agent reads every session.

slides.headline: The *template*
items: AUDIENCE: who, and what they tried
SECTIONS: in order, one line each
DONE WHEN: it works at 375px wide

slides.headline: Want the full *brief* file?
slides.body: It's in the starter pack, ready to paste.

caption:
Most "AI built me a generic site" problems are briefing problems.

If you'd hand a human designer a one-line request and expect a great page, you'd be disappointed there too. Give the agent what a good client gives you: who it's for, the sections in order, the real copy, and the visual rules.

Save this for your next build.

hook: This carousel was written by a cron job

slides.headline: This carousel was written by a cron *job*
slides.body: A teardown of the engine behind this page, and the human who still has to press approve.

slides.headline: 21:00: research and *draft*
slides.body: Claude picks the day's pillar, searches for sources, and drafts 6 to 8 slides against a written brand brief.

slides.headline: A second call *fact-checks* it
slides.body: Every claim must trace to a source or a real note. Fail twice and the day is skipped. No filler posts.

slides.headline: Puppeteer renders the *slides*
slides.body: HTML templates and one shared token file, exported as 1080 by 1350 JPEGs.

slides.headline: A human *approves* it
slides.body: An email with the slides and approve or reject links. Rejections carry a note the next draft reads.

slides.headline: 07:00: it *publishes*
slides.body: Through Instagram's API. Then it pulls saves, shares and comments at 48 hours and again at 7 days.

slides.headline: Proven formats vs one *experiment*
slides.body: 30% of posts change exactly one thing: cover, hook style, length or CTA.

slides.headline: Steal the *setup*
slides.body: The starter pack has the brief template this engine runs on.

caption:
Yes, this post was drafted by a script. No, it didn't post itself without a human looking at it.

The engine: research and draft at 21:00, a separate fact-check pass, HTML templates rendered to images, an approval email, then publishing at 07:00. Afterwards it reads saves, shares and comments and tests one change at a time.

The goal isn't more posts. It's fewer bad ones.

hook: What actually goes into a launch landing page

slides.headline: What actually goes into a launch *landing* page
Start with the *one* action
slides.body: Book a call, join a waitlist, or buy. One page, one job. Everything else is decoration.

slides.headline: Write before you *design*
slides.body: Headline, subhead, three proof points, the offer. If the copy doesn't work in a plain doc, gradients won't save it.

slides.headline: Show it *moving*
slides.body: A short loop of the product in use, near the top, explains it faster than another paragraph.

slides.headline: Build it, then check it on a *phone*
slides.body: Claude Code gets the build moving. Then go through every section at 375px wide before calling it done.

slides.headline: Homepage vs *launch* page
items: Written for everyone | Written for one visitor
Redesigned forever | Done when it converts

slides.headline: Want one built for your *launch*?
slides.body: Launch videos and landing pages by Studio FX.

caption:
A launch page isn't a small homepage. It's one argument for one action.

The order that works: decide the action, write the copy, add something that moves, build, then check every section on a phone. Design comes after the words, not before.

If you've got a launch coming and want the video and page handled, DM LAUNCH.

hook: Signs your side project is a hobby now

slides.headline: Signs your side project is a *hobby* now
More rewrites than *links* shared
slides.body: The landing page has had five headlines and zero visitors who weren't you.

slides.headline: "Just one more *feature*"
slides.body: Features don't find users. Posts, DMs and slightly awkward asks do.

slides.headline: You track tasks, not *conversations*
slides.body: A to-do app full of ticked boxes and zero replies from a buyer is a hobby with extra steps.

slides.headline: Hobby vs *business*
items: Builds what's fun | Builds what's asked for
Waits for ready | Ships, then fixes

slides.headline: Turn it back into a *project*
slides.body: The starter pack starts with the first ask, not the first feature.

caption:
Nothing wrong with a hobby. Just be honest about which one you're running.

If the roadmap keeps resetting every time a new tool drops, and the only visitor to the landing page is you, it might be time to send one awkward message instead of building one more feature.
